note: Orient the board so increasing i is east and decreasing j is south. Initially holes are the vertices of E^(m-1)S^(n-1). A move from (i,j) to (i+1,j+1) replaces holes at (i,j+1),(i+1,j+1),(i+1,j) by holes at (i,j+1),(i,j),(i+1,j), hence flips ES to SE. Conversely, an SE adjacent pair in any noninitial word has the southwest, northwest, southeast vertices empty and the northeast square occupied (it is off the path); moving that northeast coin southwest is the reverse of a legal move. Each reverse flip decreases the number of S-before-E inversions by one, so reaches E^(m-1)S^(n-1). Thus configurations biject with E/S words and number binomial(m+n-2,m-1).
